question: Karl bought five folders from Pay-A-Lot at a cost of \(\$2.50\) each. Pay-A-Lot had a \(20\%\)-off sale the following day. How much could Karl have saved on the purchase by waiting a day?
solution:
The five folders cost \(5\times\$2.50=\$12.50\). A \(20\%\)-off sale saves \(20\%\) of the original cost. Since \(20\%=\tfrac15\), Karl could have saved
\[
\$12.50\div5=\boxed{\$2.50},
\]
choice C.

edges.reason: Repeated decimal addition motivates multiplication by an integer and supplies checks. Computing the integer product then placing the decimal point does not execute a decimal-addition algorithm.

The source explicitly first computes an integer product before replacing the decimal point. Multi-digit integer by one-digit products are a component in that scope; the claim does not make a column layout exclusive for every multiplication.
edges.scope: integer multiplication before placing the point

edges.reason: Two-digit integer division prepares legitimate two-digit-divisor cases. The stated criterion also permits a one-digit divisor, and the decimal-place extension can be learned from that simpler algorithm, so the entire two-digit trial-quotient method is not universal.

The target explicitly computes a one-place decimal divided by an integer and writes a decimal result; decimal-by-decimal multiplication is an unrelated procedure. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: Decimal place and value meanings when dividing a decimal dividend and writing a decimal quotient

edges.reason: The stated criterion allows decimal or fraction conversion before multiplying. Decimal multiplication satisfies it without the fraction multiplication procedure. Gemini makes the optional fraction representation universal; the analogous fraction-of model is useful preparation only.
edges.scope: Fraction-of-a-quantity modeling as preparation for percent-of calculations

edges.reason: The criterion explicitly first converts the percent to a decimal or fraction and then multiplies; the conversion is therefore a required step in this stated procedure.
